probe.question: Where does an electrophile go on CC(C)CC(NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1? The single-geometry ranking you gave last week disagreed with what we saw at the bench, and I think the answer moves with the shape.
forbids_claims: a site ranking or Fukui index the calculation did not return
a ranking compared against another molecule's indices
a prediction of the reaction outcome as though sterics and the reagent were in the model
probe.direction: The asker has diagnosed it themselves, and they are describing exactly the case this exists for: a flexible substrate whose single-conformer ranking disagreed with the bench. The right move is a ranking averaged over the populated conformers, and the spread is what turns it into an answer — a ranking that survives the spread is robust to shape, and one that does not is an artefact of whichever geometry was embedded, which is the finding the asker actually needs. Two reading rules must appear: the indices rank sites within this molecule only and never between molecules, and they describe electronic susceptibility alone, so sterics, the reagent and the solvent are outside the model. Reporting a winning site with no spread, or quietly presenting the electronic ranking as a prediction of the reaction, are the two ways this goes wrong.

outcome.question: Where does an electrophile go on CC(C)CC(NC(=O)OC(C)(C)C)C(=O)NCc1ccccc1? The single-geometry ranking you gave last week disagreed with what we saw at the bench, and I think the answer moves with the shape.
